system.summary: Schilling-family vertical-bigram cipher over a 31-symbol Russian alphabet (28 letters, space dash, comma, full stop) written in paired 24-sign rows and enciphered column by column with three-digit codes alternating between Rank 1 and Rank 2, transmitted in two-digit pairs.
system.sibling_key: Key No. 381 instructions and worked example (frames 780, 788, 790-792) and filmed tables of Key No. 404 (frames 1440 ff.) establish the procedure and 31-symbol alphabet; their numerical tables are different keys.
system.notes: Theoretical capacity is 2 x 961 = 1,922 vertical bigrams across Ranks 1 and 2 (within 2 x 1,000 three-digit addresses); 664 distinct valid (rank, code) pairs occur in these six letters, of which 472 are assigned in key375.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary consular decipherment worksheets for Nos. 5078 and 5015 (frames 758, 772), clean copy of No. 3902 (frame 753), Russian notes for Nos. 4945 and 4166 (frames 754, 745), and Olarovsky's draft for No. 519 (frame 736) in NARA M1486 roll 83. No table of key No. 375 had been published; Michael Brackx (issue #167) described the stencil rules and noted frame 753 as a probable match for No. 3902.

conditions.human_role: Andrei Aleksandrov orchestrated the multi-stage workflow between OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and Google Gemini, enforced frozen holdout checkpoints before extending the key to Nos. 519 and 4166, spot-checked manuscript lines and disputed crops, and prepared the submission.
tools: targets/nyconsulate1891/reproduce.py (deterministic decoder, bijectivity audit, and 9,999-permutation holdout check)
finite-state alignment with spellout normalization for Russian numerals and pre-1918 orthography

solution.what: Retrieved NARA RG 64 M1486 Roll 83 scans (NAID 571170362) from catalogue 756 and Michael Brackx's issue #167 note. Verified the 31-symbol alphabet, 24-column paired-row grid, and alternating Rank I / Rank II vertical bigram mechanics from the filmed Key 381 instructions (frames 780-792) and Key 404 sample table (frame 1440). The contemporary worksheets and clear copies on frames 758, 772, 753, and 754 were inspected upfront for Stage 1.

Aligned the March 1895 consular worksheets (frames 758 and 772) directly against the two-digit transcriptions of Nos. 5078 and 5015 to establish the direct-witnessed K skeleton, then ran constrained finite-state alignment against frame 753 (No. 3902) and frame 754 (No. 4945) to build an initial 400-entry table.

Applied the frozen 400-entry table to Consul General Olarovsky's cipher reply No. 519 (frames 733-735). Prior to fitting the second half of the letter, tested the phrase 'за время моего управления' selected from draft frame 736: all 13/13 covered characters matched (0/9,999 random permutations across the second half). Constrained alignment with No. 519 expanded the frozen table to 471 entries (285 K + 186 A).

Locked 'на письменном вашем заявлении' from frame 745 (preregister.txt) before fitting No. 4166 (frames 742-743). Frozen 471-entry lookup scored 11/14 (6/8 K-only) at cell 199 on the initial 198-group transcript; inspecting the full-width NARA scan of frame 743 restored four clipped line-initial groups (00, 24, 22, 49) and 742_L01 g14 = 74, raising the frozen holdout match to 15/15 (9/9 K-only; 0/9,999 within-rank permutations).

Evaluated candidate key extensions via leave-one-out historical partitions: single-manuscript proposals scored 10/11 (90.9%, below the 95% bar) and were rejected; a two-manuscript requirement scored 24/24 (100%) and promoted only I/726 = шт and I/692 = еа (shared by Nos. 4166 and 3902), while quarantining conflicted II/925, II/494, II/249, and II/506.

In issue #803, Daniel Bourdeau reproduced all counts with a clean-room decoder and checked ~861 groups on frames 751, 752, 732, and 742, identifying 751_L06 g12 = 76, 752_L04 g6 = 79 (giving II/179 = мт), and 732_L06 g13 overwritten. Cross-checking with Brice Dudout's independent unpublished table (464/468 = 99.1% agreement) settled 757_L05 g16 = 78 (moving яв from I/387 to I/787 and decoding No. 3902 token 399) and frame 753 line 6 'предлагается' (updating I/528 to рт and resolving all 6/6 occurrences of II/925 = те), bringing whole-triple coverage to 980/1249 (641 direct K).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Partial table of Key No. 375 (472 of 1,922 theoretical vertical bigrams) rebuilt from the contemporary decipherment worksheets and clear/draft texts filed beside the cipher sheets in NARA M1486 roll 83; under the 95% sure-word rule the six mechanical decodes remain at 17%-75% whole words (~46% overall), so the texts are decoded, not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reproduce.py over 3902_decode.txt..4166_decode.txt: 980 of 1,249 three-digit vertical-bigram tokens decoded in full from key375.tsv (641 from direct K entries). Counting sure whole words only (Daniel Bourdeau, issue #803), the six letters are ~31%, 43%, 75%, 68%, 27%, and 17% (~0.46 overall).

texts.label: Circular No. 3902, St Petersburg to New York, 1/13 August 1891 (frames 751-753)
texts.summary: Informs Consul General Olarovsky that circular No. 3893 (in key No. 336) asked for the return of key No. 336, whereas the circular of 28 June 1888 (sent twice as Nos. 3313 and 3887, mistakenly in key No. 356) announced that cipher No. 375 entered general service on 1 January 1889.
texts.note: 316/417 whole triples decoded (75.78%, 135 direct K); ~31% sure whole words under the mechanical table.

texts.label: Circular No. 4945, St Petersburg to New York, 22 February 1895 (frames 732, 754)
texts.summary: Announces that key No. 381 enters general service in July 1895 and asks that withdrawn keys Nos. 356 and 375 be returned after 1 July by safe opportunity or Russian post.
texts.note: 40/60 whole triples decoded (66.67%, 24 direct K) on the extant 60-triple sheet; ~43% sure whole words.

texts.label: Circular No. 5078, St Petersburg to New York, 22 March 1895 (frames 755-758)
texts.summary: Reiterates that enciphered dispatches must end with an obligatory full stop or full stop and dash, and instructs clerks not to pad final telegraphic groups of three or five digits with leading digits or zeroes.
texts.note: 257/268 whole triples decoded (95.90%, 252 direct K); ~75% sure whole words.

texts.label: Dispatch No. 5015, St Petersburg to New York, 10 March 1895 (frames 769-772)
texts.summary: Rebukes the New York Consulate for prematurely taking on the return of keys Nos. 356 and 375 formerly held by Mr Artsimovich while both keys were still in active service.
texts.note: 118/128 whole triples decoded (92.19%, 114 direct K); ~68% sure whole words.

texts.label: Dispatch No. 519, Consul General Olarovsky (New York) to St Petersburg, 5/17 April 1895 (frames 733-736)
texts.summary: Acknowledges Circular No. 4945, promises to return cipher No. 375 at the first opportunity after 1 July 1895, and states that cipher No. 356 was never held at the New York Consulate General during Olarovsky's tenure.
texts.note: 192/242 whole triples decoded (79.34%, 82 direct K); ~27% sure whole words.

texts.label: Dispatch No. 4166, St Petersburg to New York, 18 February 1893 (frames 742-747)
texts.summary: Inquires about the unfulfilled return of all old San Francisco cipher keys handed over with keys Nos. 356 and 375 to Mr Hansen in New York for delivery to Washington, as noted on Olarovsky's written declaration of 28 November 1890.
texts.note: 57/134 whole triples decoded (42.54%, 34 direct K); ~17% sure whole words; frozen 471-entry table matched 15/15 on the locked phrase 'на-письменном-вашем-заявлении' (0/9,999 shuffles).

outcome.notes: First published partial table of Imperial Russian Foreign Ministry cipher No. 375 (472 entries: 240 Rank 1, 232 Rank 2; 285 directly attested K, 187 source-aligned A), reading 980/1,249 three-digit vertical-bigram triples across six dispatches (1891-1895). Catalogue 756 stays open for No. 5012 and the later 1906-1910+ circulars on Roll 83.
